description:
STEP 1 (build beside the old). The construction machinery. Touches nothing that exists; fully unit-tested.

Model (proposal.html sec.1-3): a type variable is a structural ADDRESS. param i -> a{i}; result -> r0; component j of the slot at address P -> P_j (param 1 field 0 -> a1_0); nesting extends the path. A name maps to the address of its FIRST occurrence; repeats reuse it. Interned ALL THE WAY DOWN: every address is its own interned Ty, every composite (tuple/list/map/arrow) is its own interned Ty, and the arrow sits on top. Addressing canonicalizes variable identity at the binder; interning (hash-consing) canonicalizes structure; together = one integer per alpha-equivalence class, by construction.

Deliver: addressed-var constructors (param_alpha(i)->a{i}, result_alpha->r0, child address P_j), the addressed-arrow builder over Types, interned leaf + composite + arrow.

Acceptance (unit tests, proposal Adoption step 1):
- (a,b) and (a,a) are DISTINCT interned arrows (this is the conflation defeated by construction).
- flibble(t,t)::t builds (a0,a0)->a0; foo(a,{b,c},d) builds (a0,{a1_0,a1_1},a2)->r0.
- input<->result identity preserved: (a,b)->b stays (a,b)->b, never (a,b)->a.
- Address, not sequence: in foo(a,{b,c},d), d is a2 regardless of how many fields the tuple has; adding a tuple field never renumbers d.
- Repeated name unifies across depth: g(t,{t,u}) -> (a0,{a0,a1_1})->r0.

Checks: cargo test --lib for the new module; zero warnings.
title: Addressed type-variable + addressed-arrow interning (constructors + builder)
